lines.text: One wrong number… and the whole AI training crashes.
AI learns by walking downhill. Up high, it's very wrong. Down low, less wrong. And the very bottom — that's the right answer.
At every step, it checks the slope and multiplies it by one number — the learning rate. That number decides how big each step is.
Too small? It inches along… and barely gets anywhere.
Just right? It lands right on target.
Too big? It bounces wall to wall… and flies right out.
Same problem. Only one number changed.
That's why big models like GPT-3 don't stick to one number. They warm up slowly, peak, then slow down.
Comment a learning rate, and I'll run yours in the next reel.
